M2: apogee <= 600 km including dispersion (MIS-COV-03, ISED propulsion threshold)

screened.F: fails M1: ground track and +-30 deg roll reach only about 55 N at 420 km [Calculated: 51.6 deg + 2.2 deg roll reach + 1.2 deg half swath]; scored below for teaching only

Coverage of 45-68 N sites (roll +-30 deg.rationale: O1 and O3 scene counts are the primary MOEs; equal to the other science criteria.

Illumination at overpass (sun elevation.scale: 5 > 45 deg in fire and break-up and > 20 deg in October; 1 terminator orbit
Illumination at overpass (sun elevation.rationale: Optical-only payload; weighted lower than coverage because A-D differ by < 2 deg.

Same-morning matchups with Sentinel-2 /.scale: 5 node within 30 min of S2 (10:30) and Landsat (about 10:12); 2: > 2 h apart; 1: no near-coincident looks
Same-morning matchups with Sentinel-2 /.rationale: O4 is the central question of the mission; cross-calibration quality depends on near-simultaneous references.

Data return (union contact time, four si.rationale: Data return is the binding constraint (research: mission analysis R2).

Disposal robustness without the sail.scale: 5 compliant without sail in all cycles; 4: all cycles with small margin; 3: strong cycle only; 2: borderline in strong cycle only; 1: never
Disposal robustness without the sail.rationale: The sail is the single compliance item (RSK-002); an orbit that does not depend on it is worth as much as data return.

Orbit life covers the 3-year design life.scale: 5 natural life > 4 y in a strong cycle; 3: about 3 y; 1: < 2 y
Orbit life covers the 3-year design life.rationale: Needed for 24 months of science after commissioning; lower weight because A, B, D, E all pass.

Launch availability.scale: 5 frequent rideshares; 3 occasional; 1 rare  [Assumed: no manifest survey yet]
Launch availability.rationale: Programmatic; weight limited because the scores are assumptions.

Licensing margin (600 km apogee rule).scale: 5 >= 40 km below 600 km; 4: 10-40 km; 1: above 600 km

evidence_by_criterion.Coverage of 45-68 N sites (roll +-30 deg: 590 km: 12.2-14.5 looks/month (calc/orbit4.py). Roll reach scales with altitude: 341/318/289 km at 590/550/500 km [Calculated] -> B about 11.4-13.5, C about 10.4-12.3 [Estimated by reach scaling]. F: see screening.
evidence_by_criterion.Illumination at overpass (sun elevation: Sun elevation 43-57 deg (break-up), 46-60 (fire), 17-32 (October) for LTDN 10:30; LTAN 13:30 within 2 deg (research: mission analysis §1.5); dawn-dusk near the terminator.
evidence_by_criterion.Same-morning matchups with Sentinel-2 /: Sentinel-2 mean local time 10:30 descending (ESA orbit description); Landsat 8/9 about 10:12-10:13 descending (Landsat 9 under-fly paper). 13:30 is 3 h later: cloud and ice change.
evidence_by_criterion.Data return (union contact time, four si: Union minutes/day [Calculated, v2 calc/trade_calcs.py]: 590 km 125.7, 550 km 117.6, 500 km 105.9, 590 km LTAN 13:30 125.7; dawn-dusk not run (contacts depend on altitude, the 13:30 run shows local time does not change them). F: Inuvik (68.4 N) never visible, Yellowknife/Iqaluit at the edge [Calculated visibility circle 12.5 deg].
evidence_by_criterion.Disposal robustness without the sail: Lifetime without sail, A_eff 0.08 m2, nominal / weak cycle, strong cycle at 0.12 m2 [Calculated, v1 decay model, v2 run]: 590 km 14.7 / 20.7 / 5.0 y; 550 km 6.0 / 10.8 / 4.1 y; 500 km 4.1 / 4.8 / 3.1 y. With the sail: 590 km 3.0/3.4 y (v1 3.0/3.4, reproduced).
evidence_by_criterion.Orbit life covers the 3-year design life: Shortest natural life (strong cycle, 0.12 m2): 590 km 5.0 y, 550 km 4.1 y, 500 km 3.1 y [Calculated]: at 500 km the last months of a 3-year life fall below 400 km.
evidence_by_criterion.Launch availability: [Assumed] SSO rideshares cluster at 500-600 km with late-morning nodes; afternoon and dawn-dusk slots are rarer; station deployment is frequent. Action: manifest survey before PRR.
evidence_by_criterion.Licensing margin (600 km apogee rule): ISED April 2026 condition (research: mission analysis R7): propulsion above 600 km apogee; 590 km leaves 10 km for injection dispersion.

state.dissent: A disposal-first view would weight the no-sail lifetime above data return and select B; recorded, and covered by the 550-600 km acceptance range.
risks_of_selected: RSK-002 (sail is the compliance item at 590 km)
state.recommendation: Keep A (590 km, LTDN 10:30) as the nominal request. B (550 km) scores within 0.05: accept 550-600 km as the acceptable injection range in the launch request (proposed change ECP-02 to SEG-LS-02), which keeps data return >= 117 min/day and halves the no-sail lifetime in a strong cycle. evidence_by_criterion.Orbit fit to T-M01 (altitude, node, incl: Rideshare node set by the primary (research: mission analysis R14); dedicated cluster chooses its orbit; station orbit 51.6 deg.
evidence_by_criterion.Schedule robustness and re-booking: [Assumed] frequent SSO rideshares; small launchers have had schedule slips; agency auxiliary slots are rare. MIS-IF-01 (two deployer designs) reduces re-booking cost.

state.title: End-to-end data architecture

option_labels.A: On-board ROI and quicklook selection + lossless CCSDS 121 + UHF store-and-forward to 4 stations; L1/L2 on ground (baseline)
option_labels.B: On-board Level-2 index maps only (burn index, ice class), downlinked over UHF
option_labels.C: Full frames with on-board lossy compression (about 8:1) over UHF
option_labels.D: Full frames, lossless, over a new S-band downlink to 4 dishes

must: M1: L1 radiometric products reach the ground for cross-calibration (MIS-SCI-09, O4)

screened.B: fails M1: no L1 radiances on the ground, so O4 (repeatability against Sentinel-2/Landsat) cannot be measured

Science volume delivered vs 13 MB/day.scale: 5 >= 2x the target area; 4 target with > 30 % margin; 3 target with 10 %; 1 below target

Radiometric fidelity for cross-calibrati.scale: 5 lossless L1; 2 lossy artefacts above 1 %; 1 no L1

On-board resources (power, processing, s.scale: 5 within current allocations; 2 needs a new unit

Spectrum and licensing.scale: 5 already in the licensing plan; 2 new band and filings

Ground segment cost and complexity.scale: 5 existing four UHF stations; 1 four new tracking dishes

Technical risk.scale: 5 flown approach; 2 new unit or algorithm with no heritage

evidence_by_criterion.Science volume delivered vs 13 MB/day: Baseline closes 13 MB/day with 38 % margin, 18 % with the worst site out (NUMBERS data_budget C1, C4).
evidence_by_criterion.Radiometric fidelity for cross-calibrati: Lossless keeps L1 radiometry; lossy wavelet compression at 8:1 adds artefacts that compete with the 5 % repeatability target [Estimated].
evidence_by_criterion.Latency for community products: Quicklooks within 24 h for >= 80 % (MIS-DAT-03); 14 windows/day, longest gap 6.6 h.
evidence_by_criterion.On-board resources (power, processing, s: L2 on board needs continuous controller operation; S-band transmitter needs several W and a pointing law [Assumed until a unit is selected].
evidence_by_criterion.Spectrum and licensing: UHF 401/450 MHz is already in the ISED pre-consultation plan (REG-SPC-01); S-band would need new filings.
evidence_by_criterion.Ground segment cost and complexity: Four UHF stations 44.4 k EUR (NUMBERS cost); S-band dishes with tracking at three unattended northern sites would cost several times more [Assumed].
evidence_by_criterion.Technical risk: Compression ratio not yet shown on mission scenes (RSK-008); on-board L2 and S-band would be new to the team.

acceptance_conditions: lossless ratio >= 1.3:1 on simulated scenes before CDR
four-site network in place (degraded case 18 % margin)
risks_of_selected: RSK-001 / RSK-010 (450 MHz uplink and radio)
state.recommendation: Keep A. It is the only option that passes both must-criteria with existing allocations. Strengthen it by verifying the compression ratio on simulated scenes before CDR (RSK-008) and keeping the 76.8 kbps growth mode above 30 deg.

analysis_conflicts.title: Single-point failure: NanoPower BP4 43 Wh (1P-4S, 12-16.8 V) — Battery capacity loss / cell short
analysis_conflicts.detail: Severity 5, RPN 20; critical because of the power subsystem. System effect: Eclipse power loss, mission loss. Downstream: AOCS, Communications, Disposal (drag sail), On-Board Computer, Payload, Thermal, Structure.
analysis_conflicts.suggested_fix: set redundancy_type='cold' (or quantity 2) on NanoPower BP4 43 Wh (1P-4S, 12-16.8 V), or accept the risk with rationale; mitigation: Cell balancing, DoD limit, redundant string, temperature control

analysis_conflicts.title: Single-point failure: ISIS AntS, 2 dipoles (401.5 / 450 MHz) — Antenna deployment failure
analysis_conflicts.detail: Severity 4, RPN 16; critical because of the ttc subsystem. System effect: Degraded link, possible loss of comm. Downstream: On-Board Computer, Structure.
analysis_conflicts.suggested_fix: set redundancy_type='cold' (or quantity 2) on ISIS AntS, 2 dipoles (401.5 / 450 MHz), or accept the risk with rationale; mitigation: Redundant release, backup antenna

analysis_conflicts.title: Single-point failure: Spacemanic Murgas UHF transceiver (401 TX / 450 RX, receive edge TBC) — Transponder failure
analysis_conflicts.detail: Severity 5, RPN 15; critical because of the ttc subsystem. System effect: Loss of commanding, mission loss. Downstream: On-Board Computer, Structure.
analysis_conflicts.suggested_fix: set redundancy_type='cold' (or quantity 2) on Spacemanic Murgas UHF transceiver (401 TX / 450 RX, receive edge TBC), or accept the risk with rationale; mitigation: Cold-spare transponder, watchdog reset

analysis_conflicts.title: Single-point failure: NanoMind A3200 (in P60 slot X3) — Processor latch-up / firmware corruption
analysis_conflicts.detail: Severity 4, RPN 12; critical because of the obc subsystem. System effect: Loss of control, safe mode. Downstream: AOCS, Communications, Disposal (drag sail), EPS, Payload, Thermal, Structure.
analysis_conflicts.suggested_fix: set redundancy_type='cold' (or quantity 2) on NanoMind A3200 (in P60 slot X3), or accept the risk with rationale; mitigation: Latch-up protection, watchdog, dual-bank firmware

analysis_conflicts.title: Single-point failure: NanoPower P60 (Dock + ACU-200 + PDU-200) — Power converter / distribution failure
analysis_conflicts.detail: Severity 5, RPN 10; critical because of the power subsystem. System effect: Loss of the loads on that bus. Downstream: AOCS, Communications, Disposal (drag sail), On-Board Computer, Payload, Thermal, Structure.
analysis_conflicts.suggested_fix: set redundancy_type='cold' (or quantity 2) on NanoPower P60 (Dock + ACU-200 + PDU-200), or accept the risk with rationale; mitigation: Redundant converters, LCL protection

data_json.name: EPS_CORE

params.name: eps.flags
params.note: bitfield: UV, eclipse, charging, batt heater on, ground-WDT warn, MPPT mode

params.name: bat.temp1
params.note: pack temperatures (also needed at 1 s for charge control)

data_json.rationale_text: Power safety first: the operator judges whether the spacecraft is power-safe from this packet alone. 1 s in contact; stored at 30 s (10 s around imaging and in LEOP/Safe) so every eclipse entry and exit is resolved.

data_json.name: EPS_DETAIL

params.name: acu.ch1_voltage
params.note: 6 MPPT inputs (P60 ACU-200): wings + body faces

params.name: pdu.out1_current
params.note: 9 PDU outputs (camera, controller, ADCS, GNSS, radio, AntS, ARTICA A, bench heater, spare)

data_json.rationale_text: Per-channel solar and per-line load currents for power trending and LCL diagnosis. 1 s in contact; stored at 5 min (30 s while the payload draws peak power).

data_json.name: ADCS

params.name: adcs.mode
params.note: CubeADCS control mode (B-dot, Y-Thomson, sun, nadir, target, inertial)

params.name: adcs.est_status
params.note: bitfield: ST valid, FSS valid, MAG valid, gyro valid, EKF converged, GNSS orbit used

data_json.rationale_text: ADCS outputs only (PI ruling): mode, estimate, rates, pointing error, wheels/momentum, MTQ duty, estimator status. 1 s in contact; stored at 30 s and at 5 s inside imaging and night-SWIR windows. Per-frame attitude and PVT for geolocation go into the image metadata on the payload controller, so stored HK does not have to carry them.

data_json.name: OBC_PLATFORM

params.name: time.obt_coarse
params.note: OBT also in every packet header; here for the S9 correlation check

data_json.rationale_text: OBC health, time, TC counters, store fill and the command-loss timer. 1 s in contact.

data_json.name: TTC

params.name: ttc.flags
params.note: TX on, beacon on, carrier lock, bit lock, frame lock

params.name: ttc.rs_corrected
params.note: RS symbols corrected on the uplink

params.name: ant.deploy
params.note: bitfield: 2 dipoles x (switch A, switch B)

data_json.rationale_text: Link health during the pass (RSSI, Doppler, frame counters, CLCW). Out of contact only the receiver runs, so 10 min stored is plenty.

data_json.name: GNSS
data_json.rationale_text: PVT for orbit determination and image geolocation. Receiver off in LEOP/Safe/Survival (modes.yaml), so the SID is disabled there.

data_json.name: PAYLOAD
data_json.rationale_text: Payload controller and camera health, product counters for the downlink choice. 10 s stored during acquisitions (exposure and FPA temperature per frame pair are in the image metadata).

data_json.name: THERMAL
data_json.rationale_text: PI ruling: thermal only once per minute, in contact and stored. Thermal time constants of a 3U are minutes; 60 s resolves an eclipse entry.

data_json.name: FDIR

params.name: mon.check_state1
params.note: ST[12] check states, 2 bits x 64 monitors

data_json.rationale_text: Monitoring and FDIR state; the events themselves come as ST[5] reports (allowance below).

data_json.name: DEPLOY_DISPOSAL

params.name: sail.timer_left
params.note: independent 90-day timer, read through an isolated interface

data_json.rationale_text: Deployment and disposal evidence (ISED disposal condition): 4 s while something is deploying (LEOP, EOL), slow otherwise.

data_json.name: BEACON
data_json.rationale_text: Bootloader lifeline on the 1.2 kbps beacon tier whenever the main TM chain is not radiating (LEOP, Safe, Survival, Commissioning before the first pass). Not stored: its content is inside SIDs 1/4/5/101/104.

data_json.name: ADCS_DIAG

params.name: model.b_ref1
params.note: IGRF model field in body frame

data_json.rationale_text: Raw sensors, estimator internals and controller terms. Off by default; enabled by TC(3,5) (and TC(15,x) store routing) for commissioning, calibration, anomaly investigation and wheel-health checks.
data_json.obcp: disable SID 20 and 120 after one orbit

functions.name: Acquire imagery
functions.description: Collect simultaneous NIR and SWIR images of a commanded target, time-tagged to GNSS time.

functions.name: Process and store on-board data
functions.description: Turn frames into downlinkable products and hold them, with housekeeping, until downlinked.

functions.name: Communicate with the ground
functions.description: Two-way encrypted UHF link: telecommand, telemetry, files, beacon.

functions.name: Determine and control attitude
functions.description: Point and stabilise the payload and arrays.

functions.name: Determine time and position
functions.description: GNSS position, velocity and time; on-board time and orbit propagation.

functions.name: Generate, store and distribute power
functions.description: Electrical power for every mode for the design life.

functions.name: Control temperatures
functions.description: Keep every unit within limits in all modes and node times 09:30-13:30.

functions.name: Manage the spacecraft
functions.description: Modes, stored plan, housekeeping, command routing, software maintenance.

functions.name: Protect the mission
functions.description: Fault management, security, compatibility and survival of the environment.

functions.name: Launch, separate and deploy
functions.description: Reach the operational orbit and become a deployed spacecraft.

functions.name: Dispose at end of life
functions.description: Re-enter within 5 years with >= 90 % probability, independently of the OBC.

functions.name: Operate from the ground
functions.description: Plan, command, track, monitor and keep the mission licensed and safe.

functions.name: Produce and deliver products
functions.description: Calibrated, validated, openly delivered fire and ice products with stated uncertainty.

functions.name: Collect NIR radiance (865 nm band)
functions.description: VNIR camera, 50 mm lens, 875/50 filter.

functions.name: Collect SWIR radiance (1610 nm band)
functions.description: SWIR camera, 35 mm f/1.4 lens, 1610/90 filter.

functions.name: Synchronise and time-tag frames
functions.description: Both cameras exposed together and every frame tagged in GNSS time.

functions.name: Control exposure and gain
functions.description: Seasonal exposure table, gain modes, night long exposure.

functions.name: Acquire calibration frames
functions.description: Dark frames, hot-pixel maps, night dark frames.

functions.name: Keep the optics clean and co-aligned
functions.description: Bench stiffness and thermal stability, contamination control.

functions.name: Extract regions of interest and quicklooks
functions.description: ROI 15 km pairs on the 60 m grid; 480 m quicklooks.

functions.name: Store products with integrity protection
functions.description: 8 GB store, per-file CRC, scrubbing.

functions.name: Transfer product files to the on-board computer
functions.description: CSP over CAN, >= 100 kbit/s.

functions.name: Store housekeeping and events
functions.description: Packet stores for HK, events, ADCS diagnostics.

functions.name: Queue the downlink by store, time window and priority
functions.description: Per-pass selection of delayed HK vs payload data.

functions.name: Apply link security
functions.description: CCSDS SDLS authenticated encryption, anti-replay, key sets.

functions.name: Frame and code telemetry
functions.description: CCSDS TM frames, RS(255,223), ASM, randomisation.

functions.name: Transmit the downlink at a selectable rate
functions.description: 401-402 MHz, 1.2-38.4 kbps ladder.

functions.name: Transmit the beacon
functions.description: 1.2 kbps beacon in LEOP, Safe, Survival.

functions.name: Deliver files with retransmission
functions.description: Acknowledged file delivery of payload products.

functions.name: Radiate and receive (antennas)
functions.description: Deployable dipoles tuned to 401.5 and 450 MHz.

functions.name: Detumble after separation
functions.description: B-dot, 10 deg/s to < 0.5 deg/s.

functions.name: Determine attitude
functions.description: Star tracker, sun sensor, magnetometer, gyros.

functions.name: Hold the commanded pointing
functions.description: Nadir, sun-safe, inertial, roll target and ground-target tracking.

functions.name: Slew and settle
functions.description: Roll up to +-30 deg, settle in 60 s.

functions.name: Manage momentum
functions.description: Magnetic desaturation.

functions.name: Report AOCS outputs
functions.description: 1 Hz outputs to the OBC; diagnostic SID on request.

functions.name: Determine position and velocity
functions.description: GNSS receiver (in the AOCS subsystem).

functions.name: Distribute PPS and time
functions.description: PPS to the OBC and the payload controller.

functions.name: Maintain on-board time
functions.description: CUC on-board time, correlation to GNSS, holdover.

functions.name: Propagate the orbit without a fix
functions.description: On-board propagator for 48 h.

functions.name: Generate power
functions.description: Two deployable wings and four body panels.

functions.name: Store energy
functions.description: 43 Wh Li-ion battery.

functions.name: Regulate and distribute protected power
functions.description: Switched, current-limited lines, latch-up protection.

functions.name: Shed loads on low state of charge
functions.description: Three thresholds: payload off, Safe, Survival.

functions.name: Inhibit power during launch
functions.description: Deployment switches and remove-before-flight pin.

functions.name: Passivate the battery
functions.description: Permanent isolation from the arrays at end of life.

functions.name: Reject heat
functions.description: Radiator coating, straps.

functions.name: Heat critical units
functions.description: Battery heater (EPS-controlled), bench survival heater.

functions.name: Limit the bench thermal gradient
functions.description: <= 2 degC between camera mounts during imaging.

functions.name: Measure temperatures
functions.description: Thermal SID once per minute.

functions.name: Manage modes and transitions
functions.description: Mode table incl. Night SWIR and EOL.

functions.name: Execute the stored time-tagged plan
functions.description: >= 48 h autonomy, >= 1000 commands.

functions.name: Collect housekeeping by SID
functions.description: PUS-C SIDs with per-SID periods.

functions.name: Route commands and data to units
functions.description: Platform data bus (SYS-IF-03).

functions.name: Accept software updates
functions.description: Image upload, CRC, golden image.

functions.name: Detect and isolate faults
functions.description: FDIR monitors, watchdog, latch-up detection.

functions.name: Recover to Safe or Survival
functions.description: Autonomous Safe entry, sun-safe pointing.

functions.name: Recover from loss of commanding
functions.description: 72 h radio power-cycle and Safe with beacon.

functions.name: Protect commands and data
functions.description: Authentication, encryption, key management, logs.

functions.name: Ensure electromagnetic compatibility
functions.description: Receiver desensitisation, RF inhibit during acquisitions.

functions.name: Survive the space environment for the design life
functions.description: Radiation dose, materials, 3 y + 6 months storage.

functions.name: Deliver the spacecraft to the operational orbit
functions.description: Procured rideshare; orbit request.

functions.name: Carry launch loads and fit the deployer
functions.description: CDS envelope, stiffness, strength, CoG.

functions.name: Deploy appendages after the separation delay
functions.description: Antennas, solar wings.

functions.name: Trigger disposal
functions.description: Authenticated command, independent 90-day timer, under-voltage.

functions.name: Release the sail through independent circuits
functions.description: Circuit A from the EPS, circuit B from the disposal battery.

functions.name: Increase the drag area
functions.description: >= 2.0 m2 sail.

functions.name: Report the disposal state
functions.description: Timer, battery, arming and deployed switches.

functions.name: Passivate after deployment
functions.description: Transmitters off, battery isolated.

functions.name: Plan acquisitions and passes
functions.description: Target plan, pass plan, flight rules.

functions.name: Command the spacecraft
functions.description: Certified operators, two-person critical commands, logs.

functions.name: Track and communicate
functions.description: Four unattended UHF stations under remote supervision.

functions.name: Monitor and resolve anomalies
functions.description: Anomaly procedure, contingency.

functions.name: Determine the orbit and screen conjunctions
functions.description: Orbit from GNSS telemetry, conjunction data messages.

functions.name: Keep licences and regulatory reporting current
functions.description: ISED, RSSSA, export, registry.

functions.name: Process Level 0 to Level 2
functions.description: L0, L1A, L1B, L1C (60 m grid), L2.

functions.name: Calibrate and cross-calibrate
functions.description: Against Sentinel-2 B8A/B11 and Landsat OLI B5/B6.

functions.name: Validate products and publish uncertainty
functions.description: dNBR validation, ice classification validation.

functions.name: Archive data and software
functions.description: 10-year archive, processing versions.

functions.name: Distribute products
functions.description: Open catalogue and community delivery per site agreement.

functions.name: Engage site communities
functions.description: Site selection, requests, feedback, data governance.

functions.name: Capture PPS and time message
functions.description: Payload controller latches the GNSS PPS and time message.

functions.name: Trigger both cameras together
functions.description: Hardware trigger, skew <= 100 us.

functions.name: Tag each frame at mid-exposure
functions.description: Time-tag convention SYS-IF-07.

functions.name: Regulatory agreements and licensing
functions.description: ISO 15288 Agreement processes; ECSS-M-ST-10C

functions.name: Quality assurance (workmanship, materials)
functions.description: ISO 15288 6.3.8; ECSS-Q-ST-10C

mode_elements.source_ref: C2O default (unit state per ConOps mode (EOSAT-1 power-line table))

requirements.text: The mission shall map burn scars and relative burn severity of boreal fires at landscape scale.
requirements.rationale: >= 40 usable cloud-free scene pairs over >= 3 burns in the first year; burn-index bias vs the dNBR-calibrated reference within 0.08

requirements.text: The mission shall explore, as an exploratory test, whether overwintering fires can be detected with SWIR at night and in early spring.
requirements.rationale: >= 10 night SWIR images over each of >= 2 previous-season burns (1 Mar - 31 May); detection or documented null result

requirements.text: The mission shall measure river- and lake-ice phenology (freeze-up, break-up, ice-on, ice-off) at community-selected sites.
requirements.rationale: one complete break-up season at >= 3 community-selected sites; ice extent for channels wider than 175 m

requirements.text: The mission shall quantify how well a low-cost student instrument reproduces Sentinel-2 and Landsat measurements and publish the uncertainty.
requirements.rationale: radiometric repeatability <= 5 %; geolocation <= 2 px after registration; >= 20 same-day matchups per product type per year; uncertainty published

requirements.text: The mission shall comply with ISED spectrum and debris conditions, the RSSSA licence, ITU procedures and export control.
requirements.rationale: all licences granted before launch; re-entry <= 5 years after end of operations with >= 90 % probability; collision probability < 0.001

requirements.text: The mission shall acquire at least 40 usable scene pairs, each with at most 20 % cloud over the region of interest, covering at least 3 distinct burn scars within 12 months of the end of commissioning.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief year-1 fire target. Verified in orbit from the acquisition log and the cloud mask (in-orbit test).
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief (science targets); research: mission analysis §6.6
requirements.acceptance: >= 40 scene pairs, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The mission shall observe one complete river- or lake-ice break-up season, from the last fully ice-covered to the first ice-free acquisition, at each of at least 3 community-selected sites between 1 April and 15 June.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief: one full break-up season at >= 3 sites. With ±30 deg roll there are 11-14 opportunities per site per month (research: mission analysis §1.4).
requirements.acceptance: >= 3 sites, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The mission shall attempt an acquisition at every opportunity within ±30 deg roll over each of at least 3 community-selected ice sites from 1 October until the sun elevation at overpass falls below 15 deg.
requirements.rationale: O3 includes freeze-up. North of 60 N freeze-up after mid-November is not observable in the optical (sun elevation 3-7 deg, research: mission analysis §1.5), so the season is bounded by sun elevation.
requirements.acceptance: >= 3 sites, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The mission shall acquire at least 10 night-time SWIR images over each of at least 2 burn scars from the previous fire season between 1 March and 31 May.
requirements.rationale: About 30 nadir and 140 roll-30 night looks per site per year (research: mission analysis §1.4). O2 is a test; a null result is an acceptable outcome (MIS-SCI-12).
requirements.acceptance: >= 10 night images per burn, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The mission shall obtain at least 20 same-day matchups per year with Sentinel-2 or Landsat 8/9 for each product type (burn, ice).
requirements.rationale: Cross-calibration and validation base for O4; Sentinel-2 shares the 10:30 descending node, Landsat crosses at about 10:00-10:15.
requirements.threshold_unit: matchups per product type per year
requirements.acceptance: >= 20 matchups per product type per year, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The mission shall deliver, for every usable acquisition over a target site, Level-2 burn-index, relative burn-severity class and ice/snow/open-water/cloud class products on a common 60 m grid.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief product list (L1/L2 chain, burn scar, burn index, ice/snow extent). The 60 m grid is where both bands meet the SNR requirement (research: payload §3.4).
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The ice-extent product shall resolve ice cover on rivers and lakes wider than 175 m (3 product pixels).
requirements.rationale: NFI brief. Resolves the lower reaches of the larger northern rivers at community-selected sites. Verified by analysis of the product MTF plus in-orbit comparison with Sentinel-2.
requirements.acceptance: <= 175 m channel width, shown by analysis in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The burn-index bias against the dNBR-calibrated Sentinel-2/Landsat reference shall be within ±0.08 over the validation set of each year.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief target. The mission's burn index is NDMI-like (865 nm / ~1.6 um) with about half the dNBR dynamic range (research: mission analysis R9): classes are reported, not dNBR-equivalent values.
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief; research: mission analysis R9
requirements.acceptance: <= 0.08 absolute burn-index bias, shown by analysis in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The radiometric repeatability of both bands shall be within 5 % (1 sigma) over any 30-day period on pseudo-invariant calibration sites.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief O4 measure; moved from payload to mission level because it depends on the instrument, calibration and processing together.
requirements.acceptance: <= 5 % (1 sigma, 30 days), shown by analysis in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The geolocation error of Level-2 products shall be at most 120 m (2 product pixels, 1 sigma) after registration to Landsat or Sentinel-2, with winter scenes over snow reported as a separate class.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief. Snow-covered scenes lack registration texture, so they are reported separately rather than excluded silently.
requirements.acceptance: <= 120 m (2 px) after registration, shown by analysis in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: Each Level-2 product shall carry a per-scene uncertainty estimate for every geophysical quantity it reports.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief: each product calibrated against Sentinel-2/Landsat with published uncertainty.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by inspection in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The science team shall report the outcome of each spring night-SWIR campaign, either detections or a null result with the detection limit in exposed hot area (m2) and temperature (K), within 6 months of 31 May.
requirements.rationale: O2 is exploratory: smouldering under snow is invisible and a 10 m2 hotspot at 800 K gives about 7 % of a daytime signal (research: mission analysis R11).
requirements.acceptance: <= 6 months after campaign, confirmed by review in RV-AR-SCI

requirements.text: The science team shall produce simulated mission Level-1 and Level-2 products from Sentinel-2 and Landsat data for every selected target site at least 12 months before launch.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief: pre-launch, simulate mission images from Sentinel-2 and Landsat. Exercises the processing chain and sets expected product accuracy before flight.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-CDR-SCI

requirements.text: The mission shall select at least 3 ice sites and at least 3 burn sites together with the northern communities concerned, documented in site agreements, before CDR.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief: sites chosen with communities. The site list drives the target database, the ground track planning and the matchup plan.
requirements.acceptance: >= 3 sites per product type, confirmed by review in RV-CDR-SCI

requirements.text: The mission shall provide at least 10 daytime imaging opportunities per month at sun elevation above 10 deg over each target site between 45 N and 65 N.
requirements.rationale: Over generic test points at 48-64 N, nadir-only gives 2.7-3.2 looks per site per month; ±30 deg roll gives 12.2-14.5 (calc/orbit4.py, calc/revisit_out.txt). Clear-sky probability is 0.3-0.5 in boreal summer, so 10 opportunities give 3-5 usable scenes.
requirements.source_ref: calc/orbit4.py (generic test points); research: mission analysis §1.4
requirements.acceptance: >= 10 opportunities per site per month, shown by analysis in AN-MIS

requirements.text: The mission shall acquire usable daytime imagery at sun elevations down to 15 deg.
requirements.rationale: Freeze-up in October at 60 N is observed at 17-25 deg sun elevation; 15 deg is the design case for open-water SNR (research: mission analysis §1.5).
requirements.acceptance: >= 15 deg sun elevation, shown by analysis in AN-MIS

requirements.text: The operational orbit shall be sun-synchronous with apogee at most 600 km including injection dispersion and perigee at least 520 km.
requirements.rationale: ISED April 2026 conditions require propulsion above 600 km apogee (research: mission analysis R7). ECP-02 (approved at SRR): the launch request asks for 590 km nominal and accepts 550-600 km; the 520 km perigee floor covers the whole range.
requirements.source_ref: ISED SMSE-009-26 (number TBC); research: mission analysis R7
requirements.acceptance: <= 600 km apogee, shown by analysis in AN-MIS

requirements.text: The local time of the daylight descending node shall be between 09:30 and 13:30 at injection and remain in that window for 24 months.
requirements.rationale: Sentinel-2 crosses at 10:30 and Landsat 8/9 at about 10:12 (descending), so a 10:30 node gives same-morning matchups (O4). The 0.15 deg injection inclination tolerance that keeps the node in the window (about 18.5 min/year per 0.1 deg) is now only in SEG-LS-02.
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief; research: mission analysis R14, §1.1
requirements.acceptance: <= 0.15 deg inclination error, shown by analysis in AN-MIS

requirements.text: The mission shall provide at least 24 months of science operations after the end of commissioning.
requirements.rationale: Two fire seasons and two break-up seasons; a third year is an extension within the 3-year design life (SYS-ENV-02).
requirements.acceptance: >= 24 months of operations, shown by analysis in AN-DEB

requirements.text: The probability that the mission completes 12 months of science operations after commissioning shall be at least 0.80.
requirements.rationale: Reliability target from the mission definition; drives single-string choices to be justified by FMECA.
requirements.acceptance: >= 0.8 probability, shown by analysis in AN-DEB

requirements.text: The space-to-ground system shall return at least 13 MB per day of compressed payload products (after lossless compression) averaged over any 7 days, in addition to real-time and stored housekeeping, with at least 10 % daily-budget margin.
requirements.rationale: Teaching baseline: 13 MB/day post-compression (open PI decision, see NUMBERS.yaml open_decisions). Four-site network: 125.7 min/day union, 25.3 MB/day of frame data at 38.4 kbps; with per-pass HK profiles the budget closes with 38.5 % margin (NUMBERS.yaml data_budget). The planned product set (10 quicklooks + 80 ROI pairs, 16.7 MB raw) needs at least 1.28:1 compression to fit 13 MB (PAY-FUN-03).
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief; research: mission analysis R2, §3.4
requirements.acceptance: >= 13 MB/day compressed payload products (7-day mean), shown by analysis in AN-DAT

requirements.text: The mission shall return on average at least 10 quicklooks and 80 region-of-interest pairs (15 km square, both bands, 60 m grid) per day.
requirements.rationale: 80 ROI pairs are 15.0 MB raw and 10 quicklooks (full frame, both bands, 480 m, 8 bit) are 1.7 MB: 16.7 MB raw, 11.1 MB at 1.5:1, inside the 13 MB/day target of MIS-DAT-01. 60 ROI pairs is the floor at the 19.2 kbps fallback rate.
requirements.acceptance: >= 80 ROI pairs per day (plus 10 quicklooks), shown by analysis in AN-DAT

requirements.text: At least 80 % of quicklooks shall reach mission control within 24 h of acquisition.
requirements.rationale: Landscape-scale seasonal monitoring, not emergency response; the longest gap without contact is 6.6 h (calc/contacts.json).
requirements.acceptance: >= 80 % of quicklooks within 24 h, measured in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: During the break-up season (1 April to 15 June) Level-2 ice products for each community site shall be delivered to the community concerned within 7 days of acquisition.
requirements.rationale: Seasonal ice information is only useful to communities while the season is under way; 7 days stays clear of emergency-response expectations.
requirements.acceptance: <= 7 days, measured in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: Every Level-1C and Level-2 product shall be released under the CC BY 4.0 licence (or an equivalent open licence) within 6 months of acquisition, except where a site agreement under MIS-IF-06 or the RSSSA licence restricts its release.
requirements.rationale: Open publication of products and uncertainties is a stated mission outcome; the RSSSA licence may restrict raw data distribution (REG-RSS-05).
requirements.acceptance: <= 6 months, confirmed by review in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: The mission shall downlink any full-frame image pair still held on board within 7 days of a request from the science team.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief: full frames on request. A full pair is 32 MB raw, about 2.4 days of the science allocation, so requests are rationed by the operations plan.
requirements.acceptance: <= 7 days from request, measured in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: All Level-0 data, products, calibration data and processing software versions shall be archived for at least 10 years after the end of the mission.
requirements.rationale: Reproducibility of the O4 uncertainty claims and long-term value of the seasonal record.
requirements.acceptance: >= 10 years after end of mission, confirmed by review in RV-AR-DAT

requirements.text: Commissioning of the platform and the payload shall be complete within 90 days of separation.
requirements.rationale: ConOps phases: LEOP 7 d, platform commissioning to L+30 d, payload commissioning to L+90 d (research: mission analysis §7.1).
requirements.acceptance: <= 90 days after separation, measured in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: The mission shall continue planned acquisitions for at least 48 h without ground contact.
requirements.rationale: Longest gap without contact is 6.6 h; 48 h covers station outages and weekends without staff.
requirements.acceptance: >= 48 h without contact, measured in TS-PFM-DITL

requirements.text: All telecommands shall originate from the single licensed mission control centre and reach the ground stations only through its VPN.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief architecture; one command origin simplifies the RSSSA Command Protection Plan.
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief (mission control in Ottawa, VPN to remote sites); RSSSA
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by inspection in IN-GS-OPS

requirements.text: The operators shall be able to choose, for each pass at any of the 4 ground stations, whether the downlink carries stored housekeeping, payload data or a set mix of both.
requirements.rationale: Telemetry design: delayed (stored) TM fills the downlink, and per pass the operators choose delayed HK or payload data across the 4 sites (pass classes in script/hk_sids.yaml).
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-BB-SYS

requirements.text: The mission shall re-enter within 5 years of the end of operational life with a probability of at least 0.90.
requirements.rationale: ISED April 2026 conditions. With the sail from 590 km: 3.0 y nominal / 3.4 y weak cycle; without it 14-42 y (research: mission analysis §2.2), so compliance rests on the sail.
requirements.source_ref: ISED SMSE-009-26 (number TBC); NFI brief; research: mission analysis §2
requirements.acceptance: >= 0.9 probability of re-entry <= 5 y, shown by analysis in AN-DEB

requirements.text: The probability of collision over the operational life shall be below 0.001 with objects larger than 10 cm and below 0.01 with objects smaller than 10 cm.
requirements.rationale: ISED conditions; assessed with ESA DRAMA/ARES or NASA DAS at PDR for the operational and the sail-deployed phases.
requirements.acceptance: < 0.001 collision probability (> 10 cm objects), shown by analysis in AN-DEB

requirements.text: The disposal action shall start within 90 days of the end of operational life, including an end of life caused by an unrecoverable anomaly.
requirements.rationale: ISED counts the 5 years from end of operational life, which includes an early failure; this is what makes the OBC-independent timer necessary.
requirements.threshold_unit: days after end of operational life
requirements.acceptance: <= 90 days after end of operational life, shown by analysis in AN-DEB

requirements.text: After drag-sail deployment is confirmed the spacecraft shall be passivated, with all transmitters permanently disabled and the battery isolated from charging.
requirements.rationale: Debris-mitigation passivation and protection of other users of 401/450 MHz after end of life.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-PFM-DEP

requirements.text: The spacecraft shall be compatible with the interface specifications of at least two different 3U CubeSat deployer designs.
requirements.rationale: Rideshare manifests slip and change; compatibility with two deployer designs allows re-manifesting without redesign (RSK-028). External interface: launch provider / deployer.
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: >= 2 deployer designs, confirmed by review in RV-CDR-LCH

requirements.text: The launch interface shall deliver to mission control the post-separation state vector or two-line elements of the spacecraft within 24 h of separation.
requirements.rationale: LEOP acquisition: with a 6.6 h longest gap and Yagi antennas, the first passes need an early orbit. Written into the launch ICD at CDR (R) and demonstrated in LEOP.
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: <= 24 h, measured in IOV-COM

requirements.text: The launch ICD, signed by the launch provider and the mission, shall define the mechanical, electrical-inhibit, environmental-test, safety and delivery interfaces before CDR.
requirements.rationale: An unsigned ICD is an assumption; NASA GEVS levels stand in until it is signed (SEG-LS-03).
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-CDR-LCH

requirements.text: Every released product shall be discoverable and downloadable by an anonymous user over HTTPS through a STAC 1.0 catalogue.
requirements.rationale: External interface to open-data users. Verified by an acceptance test of the science data system before launch.
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-GS-ACC

requirements.text: Each site community shall receive the products for its sites in the formats and languages named in its site agreement, including at least a georeferenced image and a plain-language summary.
requirements.rationale: External interface to site communities. The format and language are set with each community, not by the engineering team (validation thread V3/V6).
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: Products and data over a community-selected site shall be released, embargoed or withheld only as set out in that community's site agreement.
requirements.rationale: Governance interface. Data about community lands may fall under community data-governance principles (OCAP / CARE). Whether specific legal obligations apply (e.g. UNDRIP as adopted in Canadian law) is [Uncertain: legal question, verify with counsel]; the requirement makes the site agreement the controlling document either way.
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-CDR-USR

requirements.text: The mission archive shall be transferred to a long-term repository that assigns persistent identifiers within 12 months after the end of the mission.
requirements.rationale: A student project ends; the archive must outlive the team. External interface: long-term repository.
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: <= 12 months, confirmed by review in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: The science segment shall obtain Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 surface-reflectance and top-of-atmosphere products for every matchup through the providers' public access services, under their published licence terms.
requirements.rationale: External interface to the reference missions. Their crossing times (Sentinel-2 10:30 LTDN, Landsat 8/9 about 10:12 LTDN) drive the orbit trade T-M01.
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-CDR-SCI

requirements.text: The operator shall be registered with a conjunction-screening service, with a 24/7 contact point and ephemeris sharing at least every 7 days, at least 90 days before launch.
requirements.rationale: ISED space-safety conditions; rideshare: best-estimate orbit first, then updated with GNSS-derived ephemerides.
requirements.source_ref: ISED SMSE-009-26 (conjunction-service registration); research: mission analysis §4.2 item 11
requirements.acceptance: <= 90 days before launch, measured in TS-GS-ACC

requirements.text: Mission control shall receive conjunction data messages in CCSDS CDM format 24 h a day and supply predicted ephemerides in CCSDS OEM format to the conjunction-screening service at least every 7 days.
requirements.rationale: External interface to the conjunction-screening service; OPS-CNJ-01 acts on the messages within 24 h.
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: <= 7 days between ephemeris deliveries, measured in TS-GS-ACC

requirements.text: The mission shall use GPS L1 C/A signals as its external time and position reference, with UTC derived from GPS time using the broadcast leap-second offset.
requirements.rationale: External interface to the GNSS constellation; fixes the time scale of SYS-IF-06 and the frame time-tags (SYS-BUD-12).
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, shown by analysis in AN-PNT

requirements.text: The space and ground segments shall transmit only on the frequencies, bandwidths and powers assigned in the ISED licences, with no use of amateur-service allocations.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief: space operation service only; amateur 70 cm hardware does not cover 401 or 450 MHz anyway (research: mission analysis §5).
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief (no amateur frequencies); ISED licence
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-PFM-E2E

requirements.text: Mission control shall be able to inhibit all spacecraft transmissions within 8 h of a request from the spectrum regulator.
requirements.rationale: Regulator interface for harmful-interference cases. 8 h covers the 6.6 h longest contact gap of the four-site network [Calculated, NUMBERS ground_network].
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: interface standards / external interfaces
requirements.acceptance: <= 8 h, measured in TS-PFM-E2E

requirements.text: The stakeholder needs, measures of effectiveness and mission objectives shall be validated with a representative of each stakeholder group before PRR.
requirements.rationale: Needs validation (vv_plan V1). Communities, operators, science team, sponsor and regulators confirm the needs are theirs.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-PRR-VAL

requirements.text: Every ConOps scenario shall be traced through the requirements, and the result reviewed with operators and community representatives, before SRR.
requirements.rationale: Requirements validation (vv_plan V2): scenario tracing and a plain-language walkthrough.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-SRR-VAL

requirements.text: At least 3 site communities shall review the simulated Level-2 products of their sites and confirm or change the product definition before the acceptance review.
requirements.rationale: Pre-launch operational validation (vv_plan V3) with the simulated mission products of MIS-SCI-13.
requirements.acceptance: >= 3 communities, confirmed by review in RV-AR-VAL

requirements.text: Commissioning shall be closed only after at least 5 same-day matchups with Sentinel-2 or Landsat show both bands within the PAY-RAD and SYS-BUD-13 requirements.
requirements.rationale: In-orbit validation of products against reference imagery before the commissioning results review (vv_plan V5).
requirements.acceptance: >= 5 matchups, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: Pre-consultation with ISED on the 401 MHz downlink channel, the 450 MHz uplink and the VHF fallback shall be held before 31 March 2027.
requirements.rationale: The 449.75-450.25 MHz uplink needs RR 9.21 agreement and is the longest regulatory lead item (research: mission analysis R6).
requirements.acceptance: <= 2027-03-31 date, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-REG

requirements.text: The ITU advance publication information and the RR No. 9.21 agreement-seeking for 449.75-450.25 MHz shall be submitted through ISED at least 30 months before launch.
requirements.rationale: 4-month comment period (RR 9.3); 9.21 agreements with affected administrations (USA at minimum) may take longer.
requirements.source_ref: ITU RR 9.1, 9.3, 9.21, 5.286; research: mission analysis §4.2 item 2
requirements.acceptance: >= 30 months before launch, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-REG

requirements.text: The ISED space station licence application, including the space debris mitigation plan and Annex C link budgets, shall be submitted at least 24 months before launch.
requirements.rationale: Apply within 6 months of the ITU filing; 126-day service standard; at most two applications in process.
requirements.source_ref: ISED CPC-2-6-02 Issue 7; research: mission analysis §4.2 item 3
requirements.acceptance: >= 24 months before launch, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-REG

requirements.text: An ISED earth station licence for each of the 4 ground stations shall be granted at least 12 months before launch.
requirements.rationale: Separate licence and fee per station; 450 MHz EIRP must protect land-mobile users.
requirements.source_ref: ISED CPC-2-6-01; research: mission analysis §4.2 item 5
requirements.acceptance: >= 12 months before launch, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-REG

requirements.text: Antenna-siting and land-use consultation under CPC-2-0-03, or a documented exemption, shall be complete for each ground station at least 12 months before launch.
requirements.rationale: Rooftop or mast Yagi exemptions to be verified per site and municipality.
requirements.source_ref: ISED CPC-2-0-03; research: mission analysis §4.2 item 6
requirements.acceptance: >= 12 months before launch, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-REG

requirements.text: The RSSSA operating licence application, with the Command Protection Plan, the Data Protection Plan and the System Disposal Plan, shall be submitted at least 24 months before launch.
requirements.rationale: 180-day service standard for a complete initial application; security screening of personnel included.
requirements.source_ref: RSSSA (Global Affairs Canada); research: mission analysis §4.2 item 7
requirements.acceptance: >= 24 months before launch, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-REG

requirements.text: The PDR and CDR reports shall be sent to Global Affairs Canada within 45 days of each review.
requirements.rationale: RSSSA licence condition for systems under development.
requirements.source_ref: RSSSA licence conditions; research: mission analysis §4.2 item 7
requirements.acceptance: <= 45 days after each review, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-REG

requirements.text: Every telecommand accepted by the spacecraft shall be authenticated and encrypted as set out in the RSSSA Command Protection Plan.
requirements.rationale: RSSSA: all commands encrypted. Implemented in the OBC software, independent of the radio (OBD-SEC-01).
requirements.source_ref: RSSSA Command Protection Plan; NFI brief (uplink and downlink encrypted)
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-PFM-E2E

requirements.text: Payload data shall be encrypted on the space-to-ground link and held in access-controlled storage on the ground, as set out in the RSSSA Data Protection Plan.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief: uplink and downlink encrypted; the plan also covers ground archive access.
requirements.source_ref: RSSSA Data Protection Plan; NFI brief
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-PFM-E2E

requirements.text: The mission shall provide raw data of a sensed state's territory to that state, when the licence requires it, within 30 days of a request.
requirements.rationale: RSSSA licences include sensed-state access and data distribution conditions; confirm the period with GAC.
requirements.source_ref: RSSSA (sensed-state access, distribution); research: mission analysis §4.2 item 7
requirements.acceptance: <= 30 days from request, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-REG

requirements.text: A written export classification (ECCN) of the SWIR camera from the supplier shall be obtained before the breadboard order.
requirements.rationale: The IMX990 analogue camera is EU dual-use 6A003.b.4.a with a licence required (research: payload §1.1).
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-REG

requirements.text: Export permits for every planned transfer of the SWIR camera or the spacecraft outside Canada, including to the launch site, shall be applied for at least 9 months before the transfer.
requirements.rationale: Re-export of a controlled camera inside the satellite to a foreign launch site needs a Canadian permit.
requirements.source_ref: research: mission analysis §4.2 items 8-9; research: payload §6
requirements.acceptance: >= 9 months before launch, confirmed by review in RV-AR-REG

requirements.text: The debris mitigation assessment (lifetime, disposal reliability, collision and casualty risk) shall be performed with ESA DRAMA or NASA DAS at PDR and updated at CDR.
requirements.rationale: NFI brief commitment; feeds the ISED licence debris plan and the RSSSA System Disposal Plan.
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief (DRAMA/DAS at PDR); ISED SMSE-009-26
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, shown by analysis in AN-REG

requirements.text: The re-entry casualty risk shall be at most 1 in 10 000.
requirements.rationale: Standard debris requirement; a 6 kg aluminium 3U with COTS optics is expected to demise, to be shown with DAS.
requirements.acceptance: <= 0.0001 casualty risk, shown by analysis in AN-REG

requirements.text: The spacecraft shall release no object larger than 1 mm in orbit, with covers, pins and the deployed sail remaining attached.
requirements.rationale: Mission-related debris; the antenna and sail hold-downs must capture their parts.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by inspection in IN-EM-REG

requirements.text: The orbital data needed for UN registration shall be sent to the national registry of space objects within 60 days of launch.
requirements.rationale: Canada registers space objects through its national registry (held by the Canadian Space Agency).
requirements.source_ref: UN Registration Convention via CSA; research: mission analysis §4.2 item 10
requirements.acceptance: <= 60 days after launch, confirmed by review in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: A student-built mission that flies, trains students and delivers its science within the programme budget and schedule, on a rideshare launch.
requirements.rationale: sponsor

requirements.text: Seasonal ice-on/ice-off, break-up and burn-scar information for community-selected sites, openly published with a stated uncertainty.
requirements.rationale: user
requirements.source_ref: Northern communities that select the sites

requirements.text: NIR and SWIR imagery at about 60 m, cross-calibrated against Sentinel-2 and Landsat, with enough clear scenes over burns and ice sites.
requirements.rationale: science_pi

requirements.text: A reliable encrypted two-way UHF link, a spacecraft that runs a stored plan, organised housekeeping and a ground network that returns at least 13 MB of compressed science products per day.
requirements.rationale: operator

requirements.text: Licensable spectrum use at 401/450 MHz, disposal within 5 years with at least 90 % probability, collision risk below 0.001, command and data protection.
requirements.rationale: regulator
requirements.source_ref: ISED Canada and Global Affairs Canada (RSSSA)

requirements.text: Clear interfaces, early breadboards and a schedule that fits teaching terms.
requirements.rationale: partner

requirements.text: Calibrated fire and ice products with a stated uncertainty that they can find, download without registration and cite.
requirements.rationale: user

requirements.text: A spacecraft that meets the deployer interface and safety requirements and is delivered with its data package on time.
requirements.rationale: partner

requirements.text: Control over which of their sites are observed and how data and products about their lands are released, with their decisions recorded and honoured.
requirements.rationale: user
requirements.source_ref: Governance bodies of the site communities

requirements.text: Ice and burn information in a form and language they can use, at the time of break-up, freeze-up and the fire season, and a way to ask for sites and say whether it helped.
requirements.rationale: user

requirements.text: No lasting debris or collision hazard: the spacecraft leaves orbit within 5 years of the end of operations and shares its ephemeris.
requirements.rationale: affected
requirements.source_ref: Other operators and the orbital environment

requirements.text: Stations that have local permission, respect land use and stay within RF exposure limits.
requirements.rationale: affected

requirements.text: The space segment shall consist of one 3U spacecraft that acquires simultaneous VNIR and SWIR image pairs, stores them on board and downlinks them over UHF.
requirements.rationale: Root of the spacecraft (system-level) requirements.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-PFM-FUN

requirements.text: The space segment shall point the payload boresight to any target within ±30 deg roll of nadir and be settled for acquisition within 60 s of the start of the manoeuvre.
requirements.rationale: ±30 deg roll raises revisit from 2.7-3.2 to 12.2-14.5 looks per site per month (calc/orbit4.py); SWIR GSD is 68 x 81 m at 30 deg (research: mission analysis §1.4).
requirements.acceptance: >= 30 deg roll, measured in TS-PFM-FUN

requirements.text: The space segment shall meet its performance requirements at any circular altitude between 520 km and 600 km.
requirements.rationale: Without propulsion the orbit is set by the launch; decay before sail deployment is small but the injection range must be covered.
requirements.acceptance: >= 520 km lowest operating altitude, shown by analysis in AN-SSG

requirements.text: The ground segment shall provide at least 100 min per day of contact time, as the union of all stations above a 10 deg elevation mask.
requirements.rationale: Ottawa, Yellowknife, Iqaluit and Inuvik give 125.7 min/day (sum of sites 177.7); losing the worst single site (Inuvik) leaves 93.4 min/day (calc/contacts.json, degraded.json). 100 min/day keeps the 13 MB/day target closing with margin; with the worst single site out the budget still closes with 17.6 % margin (NUMBERS.yaml data_budget C4).
requirements.acceptance: >= 100 min/day contact (union, 10 deg mask), shown by analysis in AN-GSG

requirements.text: The ground segment shall comprise 4 UHF ground stations of a common design at generic sites near Ottawa, Yellowknife, Iqaluit and Inuvik, and one mission control centre in Ottawa.
requirements.rationale: Common design shares spares and procedures. The four sites were chosen on contact time: Inuvik adds 32.3 min/day to the Ottawa-Yellowknife-Iqaluit union (Churchill would add 0.9) and cuts the longest gap from 8.2 to 6.6 h (calc/contacts.py).
requirements.acceptance: == 4 stations, confirmed by inspection in IN-GS-GSG

requirements.text: Each ground station shall have a 401 MHz receive system noise temperature of at most 300 K, confirmed by a site noise survey before installation.
requirements.rationale: An urban site (about 700 K) leaves +0.4 dB at 10 deg with RS coding at 1 W; a quiet site gives +4.0 dB (calc/link.py). The three northern sites are rural; the Ottawa antenna is to be sited outside the urban core after the survey.
requirements.acceptance: <= 300 K system noise temperature, measured in TS-GS-SURVEY

requirements.text: Each ground station shall close the 450 MHz uplink with at least 3 dB margin at 10 deg elevation using at most 25 W at the antenna input.
requirements.rationale: +10 to +14 dB margin at 25 W and 9.6 kbps (research: mission analysis §3.3); the lowest power that closes eases RR 9.21 coordination.
requirements.acceptance: <= 25 W PA output, measured in TS-GS-ACC

requirements.text: Each ground station shall execute scheduled passes unattended, under remote supervision from mission control.
requirements.rationale: Four sites, three of them remote northern sites, cannot be staffed by a student team; operators supervise from mission control.
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief (mission control with VPN to remote sites)
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-GS-E2E

requirements.text: Each ground station shall successfully support at least 95 % of its scheduled passes in any month.
requirements.rationale: Lost passes are lost data; the 10 % availability allowance in the data budget assumes at least 95 % per site plus weather and conflicts.
requirements.threshold_unit: % of scheduled passes per station per month
requirements.acceptance: >= 95 % of scheduled passes per station per month, shown by analysis in IOV-COM

requirements.text: The three northern ground stations (Yellowknife, Iqaluit, Inuvik) shall operate from -45 to +30 degC with ice loading on the antennas.
requirements.rationale: Standard rotators are rated to about -20 degC; the northern sites need a heated heavy-duty rotator housing and the shorter 401CP14-class receive antenna. Inuvik winter minima reach about -45 degC.
requirements.source_ref: research: mission analysis §5 (northern site note); NFI ground-site choice
requirements.acceptance: >= -45 degC lowest operating temperature, measured in TS-GS-ACC

requirements.text: The links between mission control and each ground station shall run over a site-to-site VPN with mutual certificate authentication and AES-256 encryption.
requirements.rationale: Command and data protection extends to the terrestrial network; no telecommand path exists outside the VPN.
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief (VPN); RSSSA Command Protection Plan
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-EM-SYS

requirements.text: Mission control shall generate a pass schedule for all 4 stations, including the downlink content of each pass, at least 24 h ahead from the latest orbit determination.
requirements.rationale: Scheduling assigns each pass to a station and to delayed HK, payload data or a mix (MIS-OPS-04); about 14 windows per day.
requirements.acceptance: >= 24 h schedule look-ahead, measured in TS-GS-ACC

requirements.text: Mission control shall manage the spacecraft encryption and authentication keys in an encrypted key store with two-person access control, logged key loading and a documented key-compromise procedure.
requirements.rationale: The RSSSA plans need key generation, storage, change and compromise procedures; key loading before launch is a two-person action.
requirements.source_ref: RSSSA Command and Data Protection Plans; CCSDS 350.9-G (SDLS key management)
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by inspection in IN-EM-GSG

requirements.text: Mission control shall log every telecommand sent, with operator identity, time and verification result, and keep the log for the life of the licence.
requirements.rationale: Traceability of commanding for the regulator and for anomaly investigation.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-GS-ACC

requirements.text: Mission control shall deliver received payload data and housekeeping to the science segment within 60 min of the end of each pass.
requirements.rationale: Leaves most of the 24 h quicklook budget (MIS-DAT-03) to processing.
requirements.acceptance: <= 60 min after pass end, measured in TS-GS-ACC

requirements.text: Mission control shall determine the orbit from GNSS telemetry at least once per day with a predicted position error of at most 1 km 24 h ahead.
requirements.rationale: Derived from F12.5: pass prediction, antenna pointing and conjunction screening need a fresh orbit.
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: functional architecture and budget flow-down
requirements.acceptance: <= 1 km at 24 h, shown by analysis in AN-GSG

requirements.text: The spacecraft shall be compatible with a rideshare launch in a 3U CubeSat deployer, as defined in the launch interface control document.
requirements.rationale: Launch vehicle and deployer are not yet known; the CDS rev 14.1 envelope is used until the ICD is issued.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-LCH

requirements.text: The launch request shall specify a sun-synchronous orbit with nominal altitude 590 km and an acceptable injection altitude of 550 to 600 km, apogee at most 600 km including dispersion, inclination error at most 0.15 deg and a daylight descending node at 10:30 ±30 min local time.
requirements.rationale: Secondary slot: RAAN not guaranteed; the request is the only lever on apogee and LTAN drift. ECP-02 (approved at SRR): accepting 550-600 km widens the rideshare options; at 550 km the no-sail lifetime in a strong cycle is 4.1 y and contact time stays >= 117.6 min/day.
requirements.acceptance: 590 km nominal and 550-600 km acceptable injection altitude requested, apogee <= 600 km, confirmed by review in RV-PDR-LCH

requirements.text: The spacecraft shall withstand the launch environments of the launch ICD (quasi-static, sine, random, shock, depressurisation) without loss of function; NASA GEVS levels apply until the ICD is issued.
requirements.rationale: Final vibration in the deployer is done by the launch provider; the spacecraft qualifies to protoflight levels first (VER-ENV-01).
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief (final vibration by the launch provider); launch ICD (TBD)
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-PFM-VIB

requirements.text: The spacecraft shall remain in the deployer for at least 6 months without recharging and still complete LEOP.
requirements.rationale: Secondary payloads wait for the launch; battery self-discharge and the sail timer battery must allow it.
requirements.source_ref: NFI brief (launch near end of development)
requirements.acceptance: >= 6 months in deployer, measured in TS-PFM-VIB

requirements.text: The flight spacecraft and its acceptance data package shall be delivered to the launch provider at least 4 months before launch, or earlier if the launch ICD requires.
requirements.rationale: Integration in the deployer, final vibration and shipping.
requirements.acceptance: >= 4 months before launch, confirmed by review in RV-CDR-LCH

requirements.text: The spacecraft shall recover from separation tip-off rates up to 10 deg/s about any axis.
requirements.rationale: Covers typical POD tip-off; drives the detumble requirement (ADC-MOD-01).
requirements.acceptance: >= 10 deg/s tip-off rate, shown by analysis in AN-LCH

requirements.text: The science segment shall process every received acquisition through Level-0 (raw, time-tagged), Level-1A (decompressed, unpacked), Level-1B (radiometrically calibrated), Level-1C (geolocated, co-registered, 60 m grid) and Level-2 (burn and ice products).
requirements.rationale: Defined product levels make the uncertainty chain auditable for O4.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-GS-E2E

requirements.text: The Level-1C processor shall register each scene to a Landsat or Sentinel-2 reference with a residual of at most 1 SWIR pixel RMS where at least 20 tie points are found.
requirements.rationale: Pre-registration geolocation is about 1 km (0.1 deg knowledge); registration brings it to the 2-pixel target.
requirements.acceptance: <= 1 SWIR px RMS residual, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The science segment shall cross-calibrate both bands against Sentinel-2 B8A/B11 and Landsat OLI B5/B6 using spectral band adjustment factors derived from the measured flight filter responses.
requirements.rationale: the instrument bands differ from the reference bands; snow/ice reflectance is steep at 1.6 um, so SBAFs are needed.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-CDR-USR

requirements.text: The science segment shall plan at least 2 acquisitions per month over pseudo-invariant calibration sites to trend radiometric stability.
requirements.rationale: Needed for the 5 % repeatability measure; the sites are outside Canada and use spare capacity.
requirements.acceptance: >= 2 PICS acquisitions per month, measured in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The science segment shall validate the burn-index and burn-class products against dNBR from same-season Sentinel-2 or Landsat over at least 3 burns per year.
requirements.rationale: dNBR (2.2 um) is the severity standard; the mission's classes are calibrated against it.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, shown by analysis in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The science segment shall validate the ice/snow/water/cloud classification against same-day Sentinel-2 classifications and, where available, national hydrometric break-up records.
requirements.rationale: Published methods reach 89-91 % accuracy with Sentinel-2 and 3-7 day break-up date errors with MODIS (research: mission analysis §6.3).
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, shown by analysis in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: The science archive shall publish products as cloud-optimised GeoTIFF with STAC metadata, a persistent identifier per collection and the processing version of each product.
requirements.rationale: Open, findable products for communities and other researchers.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by inspection in IN-GS-USR

requirements.text: The science segment shall accept target requests from the science team and the site communities at least 72 h before the planned acquisition and pass them to mission planning.
requirements.rationale: Target database feeds the daily plan; 72 h fits the 48 h stored plan cycle.
requirements.acceptance: >= 72 h before acquisition, measured in TS-GS-E2E

requirements.text: The Level-1C resampling to the 60 m grid shall add at most 0.2 SWIR pixel RMS of registration error.
requirements.rationale: Ground-processor allocation of the registration budget SYS-BUD-13 (traced by budget_ref; a segment requirement does not take a system-level parent).
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: functional architecture and budget flow-down
requirements.acceptance: <= 0.2 SWIR px RMS, shown by analysis in AN-USR

requirements.text: After each break-up season and each fire season the science team shall record each site community's assessment of the products and the actions taken on it.
requirements.rationale: Derived from F13.6; feeds operational validation (vv_plan V6) and requirement changes.
requirements.source_ref: v2 SE pass: functional architecture and budget flow-down
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in IOV-SCI

requirements.text: No person shall send telecommands to the spacecraft before being certified as an operator through the training syllabus and at least 10 supervised simulated passes including contingency cases.
requirements.rationale: Student operators change every year; certification is also part of the RSSSA command protection.
requirements.source_ref: RSSSA Command Protection Plan; design-tool default
requirements.acceptance: >= 10 supervised simulator passes, confirmed by review in RV-AR-OPS

requirements.text: Critical telecommands (sail ARM and FIRE, passivation, key change, software image activation, transmitter disable) shall require confirmation by a second certified operator in the mission control system.
requirements.rationale: Irreversible or security-relevant commands.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-GS-E2E

requirements.text: Every nominal and contingency flight procedure shall be validated on the spacecraft simulator or the engineering model before its first use in flight.
requirements.rationale: Procedures are student-written; validation on the simulator catches wrong commands before they reach the spacecraft.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, confirmed by review in RV-AR-OPS

requirements.text: The mission planning tool shall check every plan against the flight rules (battery state of charge at least 40 % before imaging, roll at most 30 deg, no transmission during acquisitions) before upload.
requirements.rationale: Flight rules enforced by tooling rather than memory.
requirements.acceptance: statement met as written, measured in TS-GS-E2E

requirements.text: The mission planning tool shall reject any plan that starts an acquisition less than 120 s after the GNSS receiver is powered.
requirements.rationale: Flight rule derived from the timing budget SYS-BUD-12 and GNS-OPS-02: the OBD-TIM-02 holdover (1 s/day) cannot meet 1 ms, so every acquisition needs a GNSS fix.
requirements.acceptance: >= 120 s, measured in TS-GS-E2E

requirements.text: The pass plan shall downlink every stored housekeeping packet within 7 days of its generation, or record its deliberate loss in the operations log.
requirements.rationale: Per-pass choice between delayed HK and payload data must not silently lose HK when the 7-day store wraps.
requirements.acceptance: <= 7 days, measured in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: The operations team shall start the anomaly procedure for a Safe-mode entry or a missed beacon within 24 h of detection.
requirements.rationale: Passes cluster in two daily windows; 24 h always includes several passes.
requirements.acceptance: <= 24 h from detection, measured in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: The operations team shall assess and act on a high-risk conjunction alert within 24 h of receipt.
requirements.rationale: No propulsion: the actions are attitude change to minimum or maximum drag, coordination with the other operator, and reporting.
requirements.source_ref: ISED space-safety condition; research: mission analysis §6.6
requirements.acceptance: <= 24 h, measured in IOV-OPS

requirements.text: The measured launch mass of the spacecraft shall not exceed 6.0 kg.
requirements.rationale: CDS rev 14.1 3U limit and NFI brief maximum; verified by weighing the flight model.
requirements.source_ref: CubeSat Design Specification rev 14.1 (3U); NFI brief
requirements.acceptance: <= 6.0 kg, measured in TS-PFM-MP

requirements.text: At PDR the nominal mass plus equipment maturity margins (5 % off-the-shelf, 10 % modified or with a value estimated without a supplier datasheet, 20 % new) plus a 20 % system margin applied to that margined mass shall not exceed 6.0 kg.
requirements.rationale: ECSS / ESA margin philosophy. v2 classes the EXA DMSA wings as category C, 10 % (mass estimated, datasheet still requested) instead of 5 %: 4.17 kg margined, 5.01 kg with the 20 % system margin [Calculated, budgets.yaml]. The course textbook ladder allows 15 % at PDR; 20 % is held, which meets both the textbook ladder and the skill reference (>= 20 % at PDR).
requirements.acceptance: >= 20 % system mass margin, shown by analysis in AN-BUD

requirements.text: End-of-life orbit-average power generation shall exceed the orbit-average load of the nominal operations mix by at least 20 % at beta 15 deg in the nominal attitude.
requirements.rationale: Load 4.17 W orbit average (mode mix nominal 85 / imaging 5 / downlink 9 / night SWIR 1 %), 5.00 W with 20 %; deployable wings give about 12.2 W EOL; body-mounted cells alone give 4.0 W and fail at low beta (research: bus R6; calc/budgets.py).
requirements.acceptance: >= 20 % power margin (EOL), shown by analysis in AN-BUD

requirements.text: The battery depth of discharge shall not exceed 15 % in the worst-case orbit, which includes a 12 W payload acquisition of 5 min in eclipse.
requirements.rationale: Worst eclipse: 20 min nominal + 10 min downlink + 5 min imaging is about 3.8 Wh, 8.8 % of a 43 Wh BP4 (calc/budgets.py); 15 % leaves room for capacity fade and safe-mode cases.
requirements.acceptance: <= 15 % depth of discharge, shown by analysis in AN-BUD

requirements.text: The daily volume queued for downlink (payload products plus stored housekeeping) and the real-time housekeeping of the pass plan shall together be at most 90 % of the daily net downlink capacity of the 4-station network.
requirements.rationale: Net capacity 25.3 MB/day (union 125.7 min/day, 30 s acquisition per window, 90 % availability, frame efficiency 0.821). Baseline demand 15.54 MB/day gives 38.5 % margin; at the 19.2 kbps fallback the science volume must drop to about 9 MB/day.
requirements.acceptance: >= 10 % data-volume margin, shown by analysis in AN-BUD

requirements.text: The downlink and the uplink shall each close with at least 3 dB margin at 10 deg elevation to a ground station meeting SEG-GS-03.
requirements.rationale: Downlink with RS(255,223) at 1 W and 300 K: +4.0 dB; uplink at 25 W: +10 to +14 dB (research: mission analysis §3.2-3.3).
requirements.source_ref: research: mission analysis §3.2-3.3; ISED CPC-2-6-02 Annex C
requirements.acceptance: >= 3 dB link margin at 10 deg, shown by analysis in AN-BUD
